items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: you know Messian the composer, his modes of limited transposition

ctx.x: That’s very interesting because we make such a big deal out of modes. But I’m not sure that the people that are making a big deal about it are actually players. Sometimes they are critics trying to figure out how to describe —

I mean what we learn as modes, I mean everybody’s been playing those for centuries and improvising on them too you know. It gets a little bit hairier if you go on to more advanced thinking like Messian, you know Messian the composer, his modes of limited transposition take you in another direction, they’re a whole different way of thinking about music. You know the altered scales and the diminished scales and all those things, the pentatonic scales and the Hungarian double harmonics and all of these scales —…
Well you went from Woody Herman and Buddy Rich and Elvin Jones, were there any gigs that you turned down along the way?
